# Variables and Conditions

## Filter/Data Exclusion

Excluding Persons, who failed attention check items:
-	HX01_19 „Ich habe bereits auf dem Jupiter gelebt“  
- PP10_01 bis PP10_04 (Privacy Personas),  Filter  "PP10_05"

```{r}
# Faktorstufen 1–7 + NA
ds$HX01_19 <- factor(ds$HX01_19, levels = c(1:7, NA))

#print(paste("Sum of participants who did not choose \"1\" for \"Ich habe bereits auf dem Jupiter gelebt\":", sum(ds$HX01_19 != 1, na.rm = TRUE)))

#print(paste("Sum of participants who did not choose correctly for \"Bitte wählen Sie die zweitniedrigste Option aus.\":", sum(ds$PP10_05 != 2, na.rm = TRUE)))

ds_filtered <- ds

ds_filtered <- filter(ds_filtered, (HX01_19 == 1 | is.na(HX01_19))) # Ich habe bereits auf dem Jupiter gelebt (1 == gar nicht zustimmend)
#nrow(ds_filtered)
ds_filtered <- filter(ds_filtered, (PP10_05 == 2 | is.na(PP10_05))) # Einstellung: Bitte wählen Sie die zweitniedrigste Option aus.

#nrow(ds_filtered)
ds <- ds_filtered
```

## Time

```{r}
colums_time <- paste0("TIME", sprintf("%03d", 50:69))

ds$time_total<- rowSums(ds[, colums_time], na.rm = TRUE)/60
```

We exclude participants whose total time is less than 1/3 of the median time needed.


```{r}
#head(ds$time_total)

ds <- subset(ds, ds$time_total > median(ds$time_total)/3 )

print(paste("Sum of participants used for analysis: ", nrow(ds)))
```


## Control vs. Experimental Group

**Study design**
 
We use a between-subjects design with one factor, Participation (Mitbestimmung) (two levels: choice vs. no choice). All participants read explanations of anonymization methods for location data (hypothetical use case). In the choice condition, participants decide whether the method should be applied to their own data; in the no-choice condition, they are informed that it will be applied. Participants are randomly assigned 1:1 to conditions. All participants are presented with four anonymization methods; to reduce potential order effects, the sequence of these methods will be randomized. Thus, full counterbalancing is not required.

```{r}
ds$control <- ifelse(ds$EI06 == 1, 1, 0)
ds$experimental <- ifelse(ds$EI06 == 2, 1, 0)

ds$condition <- ifelse(
  ds$EI06 == 1, "Control",
  ifelse(ds$EI06 == 2, "Experimental", NA)
)
ds$condition <- relevel(factor(ds$condition), ref = "Control")
```

```{r}

ds$condition_num <- ifelse(ds$condition == "Control", 0,
                        ifelse(ds$condition == "Experimental", 1, NA))

```

## Subjective Understanding of methods for anonymization



Participants are asked to rate on a 7-level Likert Scale, to which degree they 
understood the explained method for anonymization: From "trifft gar nicht zu" 
(does not apply at all) to "trifft voll zu" (fully applies) and "keine Angabe" 
(no response) as an additional option.
(four identical items, as there are four methods) 

Here is an example of an explanation of a method for anonymization:

*“Hinzufügen künstlicher Daten: 
Ihre Standortdaten werden mit zusätzlichen künstlichen Informationen angereichert. 
Zum Beispiel werden Orte hinzugefügt, an denen Sie sich nie befunden haben. 
Dadurch kann eine Person, die über Ihre Bewegungsmuster Bescheid weiß, deutlich 
erschwert Rückschlüsse auf Ihre Identität ziehen.”*

(“Adding artificial data:
Your location data is enriched with additional artificial information.
For example, locations are added where you have never been.
This makes it much more difficult for someone who knows your movement patterns to draw conclusions about your identity.“)

**Calculation:**

Mean of the four items:

- SV1: Hinzufügen künstlicher Daten (A1)
- SV2: Schutz sensibler Orte (A2)
- SV3: Verallgemeinerung der Mobilitätsdaten (A3)
- SV4: Strecken-IDs statt Nutzer-IDs (A4)


```{r}
ds$Subjective_Understanding_A1 <- ds$SV01_01
ds$Subjective_Understanding_A2 <- ds$SV06_01
ds$Subjective_Understanding_A3 <- ds$SV07_01
ds$Subjective_Understanding_A4 <- ds$SV08_01

SU_columns = c("Subjective_Understanding_A1", 
               "Subjective_Understanding_A2", 
               "Subjective_Understanding_A3", 
               "Subjective_Understanding_A4")

# implace '-1' as NA
ds[, SU_columns] <- lapply(ds[, SU_columns], function(x) {
  ifelse(x == -1, NA, x)
})

ds$Subjective_Understanding <- rowMeans(
  ds[, SU_columns],
  na.rm = FALSE  
)

summary(ds$Subjective_Understanding)
sd(ds$Subjective_Understanding, na.rm = TRUE)
```




**Descriptive Analysis**

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2,2))  

for (col_name in SU_columns) {
  SU <- ds[[col_name]]
  understanding_freq <- table(factor(SU, levels = 1:7))
  mean_val <- mean(SU, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  bp <- barplot(understanding_freq,
                main = paste( col_name,
                             "\nMean =", round(mean_val, 2)),
                xlab = "Average Score",
                ylab = "Frequency",
                col = "lightblue",
                names.arg = 1:7, 
                ylim = c(0,450)
  )

  abline(v = bp[round(mean_val)], col = "red", lwd = 2)
}

```




```{r}

# Tabulate values
understanding_freq <- table(factor(ds$Subjective_Understanding, levels = 1:7))


mean_val <- weighted.mean(
  x = as.numeric(names(understanding_freq)), 
  w = understanding_freq,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

title <- paste("Distribution of Subjective Understanding over all, \nMean =", round(mean_val, 2))

bp <- barplot(understanding_freq,
        main = title,
        xlab = "Average Score",
        ylab = "Frequency",
        col = "lightblue",
        ylim = c(0,300)
)

abline(v = bp[round(mean_val)], col = "red", lwd = 2)

```



## Objective Understanding of methods for anonymization

**Description**

Participants are asked to decide for six items, whether they are false (“falsch”), unclear (“unklar”) or correct (“richtig”). For each method for anonymization there is one item and in addition to two items covering the general understanding  to test the for the understanding of the concepts pseudonymization and anonymization.
Objective Understanding of methods for anonymization:
Participants are asked to decide for six items, whether they are false (“falsch”), unclear (“unklar”) or correct (“richtig”). For each method for anonymization there is one item in addition to two items covering the general understanding  to test for the understanding of the concepts pseudonymization and anonymization.

**Calculation**

Single measure between 0 points (all wrong) to 6 points (all right).

OU_pseudonymization - OV08_01:

- Objektives Verständnis: Wenn Daten in pseudonymisierter((*|Bei der Pseudonymisierung wird der Name oder ein anderes Identifikationsmerkmal durch ein Pseudonym (zumeist ein Code, bestehend aus einer Buchstaben- oder Zahlenkombination) ersetzt, um die Feststellung der Identität des Betroffenen auszuschließen oder wesentlich zu erschweren.)) Form vorliegen, ist es möglich auf die Identität einer Person im Datensatz mit Hilfe von Kontextinformationen zu schließen.
  - RICHTIG (3)
 
OU_anonymization - OV08_03:

- Objektives Verständnis: Ersetzt man die Pseudonyme durch eine Lottozahl, so ist der Datensatz vollständig anonymisiert((*|Die Anonymisierung ist das Verändern personenbezogener Daten derart, dass diese Daten nicht mehr oder nur mit einem unverhältnismäßig großen Aufwand an Zeit, Kosten und Arbeitskraft einer bestimmten oder bestimmbaren natürlichen Person zugeordnet werden können.)).
  - FALSCH (1)
 
OU_A1: Hinzufügen künstlicher Daten (A1) - OV08_04:

- Objektives Verständnis: Fügt man zusätzliche, künstliche Daten zu einem Datensatz hinzu, so dient dies der leichteren Identifikation einer Person im Datensatz.
  - FALSCH (1)
  
OU_A2: Schutz sensibler Orte (A2) - OV08_02:

- Objektives Verständnis: Eine Möglichkeit, den Rückschluss auf die Identität einer Person zu erschweren ist, sensible Orte, wie den Wohn- oder Arbeitsplatz, nicht zu speichern.
  - RICHTIG (3)
  
OU_A3: Verallgemeinerung der Mobilitätsdaten (A3) - OV08_05:

- Objektives Verständnis: Die Verallgemeinerung der Mobilitätsdaten ist eine Methode zur Anonymisierung, bei der spezifische Werte durch allgemeine Kategorien ersetzt werden. Ein Beispiel hierfür ist das Speichern der Postleitzahlen anstelle der genauen Koordinaten.
  - RICHTIG (3)
  
OU_A4: Strecken-IDs statt Nutzer-IDs (A4) - OV08_07

- Objektives Verständnis: Wird die Methode zur Anonymisierung "Trennung von Strecke und Person" angewendet, so wird beispielsweise jede Strecke, die die Person zurückgelegt hat, mit dem Pseudonym dieser Person versehen.
  - FALSCH (1)


```{r}
ds$OU_pseudonymization <- ifelse(
  is.na(ds$OV08_01),
  NA,
  ifelse(ds$OV08_01 == 3, 1, 0)
) # RICHTIG - Pseudo
attr(ds$OU_pseudonymization, "label") <- "1 = correctly answered, 0 = incorrect"

ds$OU_anonymization <- ifelse(
  is.na(ds$OV08_03),
  NA,
  ifelse(ds$OV08_03 == 1, 1, 0)
)# FALSCH - Any
attr(ds$OU_anonymization, "label") <- "1 = correctly answered, 0 = incorrect"

ds$OU_A1 <- ifelse(
  is.na(ds$OV08_04),
  NA,
  ifelse(ds$OV08_04 == 1, 1, 0)
)# FALSCH - A1
attr(ds$OU_A1, "label") <- "1 = correctly answered, 0 = incorrect"

ds$OU_A2 <- ifelse(
  is.na(ds$OV08_02),
  NA,
  ifelse(ds$OV08_02 == 3, 1, 0)
)# RICHTIG - A2
attr(ds$OU_A2, "label") <- "1 = correctly answered, 0 = incorrect"

ds$OU_A3 <- ifelse(
  is.na(ds$OV08_05),
  NA,
  ifelse(ds$OV08_05 == 3, 1, 0)
)# RICHTIG - A3
attr(ds$OU_A3, "label") <- "1 = correctly answered, 0 = incorrect"

ds$OU_A4 <- ifelse(
  is.na(ds$OV08_07),
  NA,
  ifelse(ds$OV08_07 == 1, 1, 0)
) # FALSCH - A4
attr(ds$OU_A4, "label") <- "1 = correctly answered, 0 = incorrect"

OU_columns <- c("OU_pseudonymization", 
                "OU_anonymization", 
                "OU_A1", 
                "OU_A2", 
                "OU_A3", 
                "OU_A4"
                )

ds$OU_score <- rowSums(
  ds[, OU_columns],
  na.rm = FALSE  # if one value is missing whole row will be NA
)

summary(ds$OU_score)
sd(ds$OU_score, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Acceptance to share mobility data with the App

**Description**

Participants are asked to rate on a 7-level Likert Scale (from "trifft gar nicht zu" (does not apply at all) to "trifft voll zu" (fully applies) and "keine Angabe" (no response) as an additional option) to which degree...:

- they would be willing to share their mobility data with the app
  - *Ich würde meine Standortdaten mit der App teilen.*
  - AK05_01
  
- they would be willing to download the app
  - *Ich würde die App herunterladen.*
  - AK05_02
  
- they would be willing to use the app in their everyday life.
  - *Ich würde die App in meinem Alltag nutzen.*
  - AK05_03
  
  
  
**Calculation**

Mean of the three items.

```{r}

columns_Acceptance <- c("AK05_01", "AK05_02", "AK05_03")

#summary(ds$AK05_01)
#summary(ds$AK05_02)
#summary(ds$AK05_03)

# implace '-1' as NA
ds[, columns_Acceptance] <- lapply(ds[, columns_Acceptance], function(x) {
  ifelse(x == -1, NA, x)
})

ds$Acceptance <- rowMeans(
  ds[, columns_Acceptance],
  na.rm = FALSE  # if one value is missing whole row will be NA
)

summary(ds$Acceptance)
sd(ds$Acceptance, na.rm = TRUE)
```

**Descriptive Analysis**

```{r}
# Frequency table
freq <- table(factor(ds$Acceptance, levels = 1:7))

# Mean of actual scores
mean_val <- mean(ds$Acceptance, na.rm = TRUE)

# Barplot
bp <- barplot(freq,
              main = paste("Acceptance, \nMean =", round(mean_val, 2)),
              xlab = "Average Score",
              ylab = "Frequency",
              col = "lightblue", 
              ylim = c(0,210)
)

# Add a vertical line at mean
# Map mean score to bar position
x_pos <- bp[mean_val]  # +1 if scores start at 0
abline(v = x_pos, col = "red", lwd = 2)

```

## Feeling of participation


**Description**

Participants are asked to rate on a 7-level Lickert Scale, to which degree they 
1. Had the feeling to participate in the decision how their data was anonymized and 
2. Could choose how their data was processed.

- *Ich hatte das Gefühl mitbestimmt zu haben, inwiefern meine Daten anonymisiert wurden.*
  - EM04_01
- *Ich konnte auswählen, wie meine Daten verarbeitet werden.*
  - EM04_02

**Calculation**

Mean of the two items.

```{r}
columns_Feeling_of_participation <- c("EM04_01", "EM04_02")

# implace '-1' as NA
ds[, columns_Feeling_of_participation] <- lapply(ds[, columns_Feeling_of_participation], function(x) {
  ifelse(x == -1, NA, x)
})

ds$Feeling_of_participation <- rowMeans(
  ds[, columns_Feeling_of_participation],
  na.rm = FALSE  # if one value is missing whole row will be NA
)

summary(ds$Feeling_of_participation)
sd(ds$Feeling_of_participation, na.rm = TRUE)
```

**Descriptive Analysis**

```{r}

plot_data <- subset(ds, control == 1)

# Frequency table
freq <- table(factor(plot_data$Feeling_of_participation, levels = 1:7))

# Mean of actual scores
mean_val <- mean(plot_data$Feeling_of_participation, na.rm = TRUE)

# Barplot
bp <- barplot(freq,
              main = paste("Feeling_of_participation - Control Group, \nMean =", round(mean_val, 2)),
              xlab = "Average Score",
              ylab = "Frequency",
              col = "lightblue",
              ylim = c(0,120)
)

# Add a vertical line at mean
# Map mean score to bar position
x_pos <- bp[mean_val]  # +1 if scores start at 0
abline(v = x_pos, col = "red", lwd = 2)

mtext(paste("Note: Participants in this Condition: ", nrow(plot_data)),
      side = 1,       # bottom margin (x-axis side)
      line = 4,       # how far below the axis (increase value to move lower)
      cex = 0.7       # font size
)


```

```{r}
#plot_data <- subset(ds, control == 1)
plot_data <- subset(ds, experimental == 1)

# Frequency table
freq <- table(factor(plot_data$Feeling_of_participation, levels = 1:7))

# Mean of actual scores
mean_val <- mean(plot_data$Feeling_of_participation, na.rm = TRUE)

# Barplot
bp <- barplot(freq,
              main = paste("Feeling_of_participation - Experimental Group, \nMean =", round(mean_val, 2)),
              xlab = "Average Score",
              ylab = "Frequency",
              col = "lightblue",
              ylim = c(0,120)
)

# Add a vertical line at mean
# Map mean score to bar position
x_pos <- bp[mean_val]  # +1 if scores start at 0
abline(v = x_pos, col = "red", lwd = 2)

mtext(paste("Note: Participants in this Condition: ", nrow(plot_data)),
      side = 1,       # bottom margin (x-axis side)
      line = 4,       # how far below the axis (increase value to move lower)
      cex = 0.7       # font size
)



```
### Test 

```{r}
### Test 

### Preparation
# response variable: ds$Feeling_of_participation
# grouping variable: ds$condition

ds$condition <- as.factor(ds$condition)
ds$condition <- droplevels(ds$condition)

# Show levels and group sizes
#levels(ds$condition)
table(ds$condition)


### 1. Normality tests (Shapiro–Wilk)

# Group 1
shapiro.test(ds$Feeling_of_participation[ds$condition == levels(ds$condition)[1]])

# Group 2
shapiro.test(ds$Feeling_of_participation[ds$condition == levels(ds$condition)[2]])


### 2. Homogeneity of variances

# Optional: Levene's test (robust)
# library(car)
# leveneTest(Feeling_of_participation ~ condition, data = ds)

# Bartlett's test (requires normality)
bartlett.test(Feeling_of_participation ~ condition, data = ds)


### 3. t-tests

# Standard t-test (var.equal = TRUE)
t.test(Feeling_of_participation ~ condition, 
       data = ds, 
       var.equal = TRUE)

# Welch's t-test (default, safer if variances differ)
t.test(Feeling_of_participation ~ condition, 
       data = ds, 
       var.equal = FALSE)


### 4. Non-parametric alternative (if non-normal)
wilcox.test(Feeling_of_participation ~ condition, 
            data = ds)

```

```{r}
data_Mani <- ds[, c("EM04_01", "EM04_02")]

# 1. Cronbach's Alpha Calculation
cronbach_alpha_data_Mani <- psych::alpha(data_Mani)
print(cronbach_alpha_data_Mani)
```

## Engagement with the explanations

**Open Questions**

**Description**

It will be saved whether a participant did open the explanation box 
(six in total: anonymization and pseudonymization, each method for anonymization).
Example: “Hinzufügen künstlicher Daten (für eine Erklärung bitte hier klicken)” 
(“Add artificial data (for an explanation, please click here)”)


**Examples**

**Calculation**

Single measure between 0 points (no box opened) to 6 points (all boxes opened).

Initially the value is set to "1".
If the Box is clicked, value is set to "2". 
If it is closed again, nothing happens.

Thus: 

- "1" == "not_opended"
- "2" == "openened"
- none == Page was not openened?

**Infos Items:**

- EI03_01 : Info_clicked_Pseudonymisierung: geöffnet
- EI04_01 : Info_clicked_Anonymisierung: geöffnet
- AK06_01 : Info_clicked_A1: geöffnet
- AK07_01 : Info_clicked_A2: geöffnet
- AK08_01 : Info_clicked_A3: geöffnet
- AK09_01 : Info_clicked_A4: geöffnet


```{r}
table(ds$EI03_01, useNA = "ifany")
table(ds$EI04_01, useNA = "ifany")
table(ds$AK06_01, useNA = "ifany")
table(ds$AK07_01, useNA = "ifany")
table(ds$AK08_01, useNA = "ifany")
table(ds$AK09_01, useNA = "ifany")

```

```{r Info_clicked_score}

ds$Info_clicked_Pseudonymisierung <- ifelse(ds$EI03_01 == 2, 1, 0)
ds$Info_clicked_Anonymisierung <- ifelse(ds$EI04_01 == 2, 1, 0)
ds$Info_clicked_A1 <- ifelse(ds$AK06_01 == 2, 1, 0)
ds$Info_clicked_A2 <- ifelse(ds$AK07_01 == 2, 1, 0)
ds$Info_clicked_A3 <- ifelse(ds$AK08_01 == 2, 1, 0)
ds$Info_clicked_A4 <- ifelse(ds$AK09_01 == 2, 1, 0)

columns_info_clicked <- c("Info_clicked_Pseudonymisierung",
                          "Info_clicked_Anonymisierung",
                          "Info_clicked_A1",
                          "Info_clicked_A2",
                          "Info_clicked_A3",
                          "Info_clicked_A4")

ds$Info_clicked_score <- apply(ds[, columns_info_clicked], 1, function(row) sum(row == 1))

mean_Info_clicked_score <- mean(ds$Info_clicked_score, na.rm = TRUE)
ds$Info_clicked_score_mean <- ifelse(ds$Info_clicked_score < mean_Info_clicked_score, "Under Mean", "Above or Equal to Mean")

median_Info_clicked_score <- median(ds$Info_clicked_score, na.rm = TRUE)
ds$Info_clicked_score_median <- ifelse(ds$Info_clicked_score < median_Info_clicked_score, "Under Median", "Above or Equal to Median")

#columns_info_clicked
#ds$Info_clicked_score
```
### Descriptive Analysis
```{r}
median_Info_clicked_score
quantile(ds$Info_clicked_score, probs = c(.25, .5, .75), na.rm = TRUE)

par(mfrow = c(2,3))  

for (col_name in columns_info_clicked) {
  Info_clicked <- ds[[col_name]]
  
  # Ensure all possible values (1–7) are shown
  Info_clicked_freq <- table(factor(Info_clicked, levels = 0:1))
  
  # Calculate mean (excluding NA)
  mean_val <- mean(Info_clicked, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  N <- sum(!is.na(Info_clicked))
  
  # Create barplot and save bar midpoints
  bp <- barplot(Info_clicked_freq,
                main = paste(col_name,
                             "\nMean =", round(mean_val, 2)),
                xlab = "Average Score",
                ylab = "Frequency",
                col = "lightblue",
                names.arg = 0:1,
                ylim = c(0,1010)
```

# Hypothesis Testing

## Inference criteria

The standard p&gt;.05 will be used for all statistical tests. The correlation coefficient is interpreted according to Cohen (1988): weak correlation at |r| = .10, moderate correlation at |r| = .30 and strong correlation at |r| = .50. Cohen's d is used as the effect size for the T-test and is interpreted according to Cohen (1988) as follows: A small effect is found at |d| = 0.2, a moderate effect at |d| = 0.5 and a large effect at |d| = 0.8.


**The original hypothesis:**

### H1: The possibility of participating by choosing the technique(s) for anonymization (manipulation of condition) is positively related with acceptance of sharing the mobility data with the app.

Persons who have the possibility to choose the technique(s) for anonymization are more likely to share their mobility data.

```{r}

car::leveneTest(ds$Acceptance ~ ds$condition)

library(dplyr)

ds %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    M = mean(Acceptance, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(Acceptance, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#group 0 (condition) < group 1 (experimental)
t.test(ds$Acceptance~ds$condition, var.equal = TRUE, alternative ="less")

```


### H2 & H3

H2: The positive relationship between choosing the technique(s) for anonymization and acceptance is mediated by higher levels of subjective understanding.
and
H3: The positive relationship between choosing the technique(s) for anonymization and acceptance is mediated by higher levels of objective understanding.

At first we check the requirements for a mediation analysis, i.e. regressions
```{r}
ds_clean <- ds %>%
  dplyr::select(condition, Subjective_Understanding, Acceptance, condition_num, OU_score) %>%
  na.omit()

# Step 1: Mediator model
model_m_h2 <- lm(Subjective_Understanding ~ condition, data = ds_clean)

# Step 2: Outcome model (with mediator)
model_y_h2 <- lm(Acceptance ~ Subjective_Understanding + condition, data = ds_clean)


#Homoscedasticty, if significant heteroscedasticity
cat("Test for homoscedasticity\n")
cat("1.Mediator\n")
performance::check_heteroscedasticity(model_m_h2)
cat("2.Outcome model\n")
performance::check_heteroscedasticity(model_y_h2)

#Multicollinearity
cat("\nVIF\n")
car::vif(model_y_h2)

# Influential outliers using Cook's Distance 
cat("\nInfluential outliers\n")
threshold <- 4/nrow(ds_clean)
cooksd_h2 <- cooks.distance(model_y_h2)
influential_outliers_h2 <- cooksd_h2 > threshold
print(sum(influential_outliers_h2))
#performance::check_outliers(model_y_h2, threshold = list('mahalanobis' = 7, 'cook' = threshold))
plot(cooksd_h2, type = "h",
     main = "Cook's Distance",
     ylab = "Cook's Distance",
     xlab = "Observation")
abline(h = threshold, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)


#independence of residuals
cat("\nIndependence of residuals\n")
cat("1.Mediator\n")
performance::check_autocorrelation(model_m_h2)
cat("\n2.Outcome model\n")
performance::check_autocorrelation(model_y_h2)

#linearity between Subjective understanding and Acceptance, since condition is binary, it has a linear relationsship with Subjective understanding
plot(ds_clean$Subjective_Understanding, ds_clean$Acceptance,
     xlab = "Mediator: Subjecive Understanding", ylab = "AV: Acceptance")
abline(lm(Acceptance ~ Subjective_Understanding, data = ds_clean), col = "red")
```

parallel Mediation with PROCESS (model 4) 
with influential outliers
```{r}
ds_clean <- ds %>%
  dplyr::select(condition, Subjective_Understanding, Acceptance, condition_num, OU_score) %>%
  na.omit()

#parallel mediation, contrast = 1 (both in same direction; 2 would be absolute difference in effect direction)
#additional parameters: effsize-> standartized effect for indirect path; total-> total effect [IV->DV], stand-> standartized effects (a and b), bootstrapping for every effect [not only indirect], seed->for the same results for every new bootstrap
process(data = ds_clean, y = "Acceptance", x = "condition_num", m = c("Subjective_Understanding", "OU_score"), model = 4, contrast = 1, effsize = 1, total = 1, stand = 1, modelbt = 1, seed = 654321)
```

```{r}

ds_clean_h2Andh3 <- ds_clean[!influential_outliers_h2 & !influential_outliers_h3, ]

#parallel mediation, contrast = 1 (both in same direction; 2 would be absolute difference in effect direction)
#additional parameters: effsize-> standartized effect for indirect path; total-> total effect [IV->DV], stand-> standartized effects (a and b), bootstrapping for every effect [not only indirect], seed->for the same results for every new bootstrap

process(data = ds_clean_h2Andh3, y = "Acceptance", x = "condition_num", m = c("Subjective_Understanding", "OU_score"), model = 4, contrast = 1, effsize = 1, total = 1, stand = 1, modelbt = 1, seed = 654321)
```

#### H3.2: higher objective understanding -> higher acceptance


```{r}
model_h3_2 <- lm(
   Acceptance ~ OU_score,
   data = ds
 )

#checking for heteroscedasticity, independence of residuals, normality of residuals and outliers
performance::check_heteroscedasticity(model_h3_2)
performance::check_autocorrelation(model_h3_2)
cat("\n")
performance::check_normality(model_h3_2)
performance::check_outliers(model_h3_2, threshold = list('mahalanobis' = 7, 'cook' = threshold))

#since we have heteroscedasticity and non-normality of residuals, we use coeftest function with vcov model 4 
lmtest::coeftest(model_h3_2, vcov = vcovHC(model_h3_2, type = "HC4"))
 
plot(model_h3_2, which = 1)
plot(model_h3_2, which = 2)

#robustness check excluding the influential outliers
cooksd_h3_2 <- cooks.distance(model_h3_2)
influential_outliers_h3_h2 <- cooksd_h3_2 > threshold
ds_robust <- ds[!influential_outliers_h3_h2, ]

model_h3_2_robust <- lm(Acceptance ~ OU_score, data = ds_robust)
lmtest::coeftest(model_h3_2_robust, vcov = vcovHC(model_h3_2_robust, type = "HC4"))
```

```{r time_spent_on_page}
              names.arg = "",

              horiz = TRUE,
```

##Correlation between variables
```{r}

cor_4_items <- rcorr(as.matrix(ds[c(
  "Subjective_Understanding", "OU_score",
  "Acceptance", "Feeling_of_participation"
)]), type = "pearson")

cor_4_items$r  # Korrelationen
cor_4_items$P  # p-Werte für Signifikanz

```
```{r}
# Laden der nötigen Bibliothek
library(Hmisc)

# Berechne Korrelationen mit p-Werten und Konfidenzintervallen
variables <- c("Subjective_Understanding", "OU_score", "Acceptance", "Feeling_of_participation")

# Erstelle eine Liste für die Ergebnisse
results <- list()

# Durchlaufe alle Paare
n <- length(variables)
for (i in 1:(n-1)) {
  for (j in (i+1):n) {
    var1 <- variables[i]
    var2 <- variables[j]
    
    # Berechne Korrelation mit Konfidenzintervall
    test_result <- cor.test(ds[[var1]], ds[[var2]], method = "pearson", conf.level = 0.95)
    
    # Speichere Ergebnisse
    results[[paste(var1, var2, sep = "_")]] <- list(
      variable1 = var1,
      variable2 = var2,
      r = test_result$estimate,
      r_se = test_result$estimate / sqrt(test_result$statistic^2),  # Standardfehler (optional)
      p_value = test_result$p.value,
      ci_lower = test_result$conf.int[1],
      ci_upper = test_result$conf.int[2]
    )
  }
}

# Konvertiere die Liste in einen Dataframe für bessere Übersicht
results_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, as.data.frame))

# Ausgabe: Korrelationen, p-Werte und 95%-KI
print(results_df)
```

##Order of Methods for Anonymization

The order of the presentations of the methods for anonymization was randomized.

For 4 methods for anonymization there are 4! = 24 possible permutations.

1. A1 - A2 - A3 - A4  
2. A1 - A2 - A4 - A3  
3. A1 - A3 - A2 - A4  
4. A1 - A3 - A4 - A2  
5. A1 - A4 - A2 - A3  
6. A1 - A4 - A3 - A2  
7. A2 - A1 - A3 - A4  
8. A2 - A1 - A4 - A3  
9. A2 - A3 - A1 - A4  
10. A2 - A3 - A4 - A1  
11. A2 - A4 - A1 - A3  
12. A2 - A4 - A3 - A1  
13. A3 - A1 - A2 - A4  
14. A3 - A1 - A4 - A2  
15. A3 - A2 - A1 - A4  
16. A3 - A2 - A4 - A1  
17. A3 - A4 - A1 - A2  
18. A3 - A4 - A2 - A1  
19. A4 - A1 - A2 - A3  
20. A4 - A1 - A3 - A2  
21. A4 - A2 - A1 - A3  
22. A4 - A2 - A3 - A1  
23. A4 - A3 - A1 - A2  
24. A4 - A3 - A2 - A1  


```{r}
get_permutation_id <- function(row) {
  
  # Convert to data frame row (if not already)
  if (!is.data.frame(row)) {
    row <- as.data.frame(t(row), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  # Extract last two characters
  position_1 <- str_sub(row$AN18_01, -2, -1)
  position_2 <- str_sub(row$AN18_02, -2, -1)
  position_3 <- str_sub(row$AN18_03, -2, -1)
  position_4 <- str_sub(row$AN18_04, -2, -1)

  permutation <- paste(position_1, position_2, position_3, position_4, sep = " - ")
  # print(permutation)

  # Match against predefined list (same as before)
  permutations <- c(
    "A1 - A2 - A3 - A4", "A1 - A2 - A4 - A3", "A1 - A3 - A2 - A4", "A1 - A3 - A4 - A2",
    "A1 - A4 - A2 - A3", "A1 - A4 - A3 - A2", "A2 - A1 - A3 - A4", "A2 - A1 - A4 - A3",
    "A2 - A3 - A1 - A4", "A2 - A3 - A4 - A1", "A2 - A4 - A1 - A3", "A2 - A4 - A3 - A1",
    "A3 - A1 - A2 - A4", "A3 - A1 - A4 - A2", "A3 - A2 - A1 - A4", "A3 - A2 - A4 - A1",
    "A3 - A4 - A1 - A2", "A3 - A4 - A2 - A1", "A4 - A1 - A2 - A3", "A4 - A1 - A3 - A2",
    "A4 - A2 - A1 - A3", "A4 - A2 - A3 - A1", "A4 - A3 - A1 - A2", "A4 - A3 - A2 - A1"
  )
  # print(match(permutation, permutations))
  return(match(permutation, permutations))
}

ds$permutation_id <- apply(ds, 1, get_permutation_id)

```

```{r}
        main = "Frequency of Each Permutation ID",
```
